newsitem.title: UK: Overweight Poland, Hungary in emerging Europe - HSBC.
newsitem.headline: Overweight Poland, Hungary in emerging Europe - HSBC.

text.p: HSBC James Capel, in a new report, recommends that investors take an overweight position in Hungary and Poland within the emerging European equity category.
The recommendation appears in the November issue of the bank's Emerging Europe Investment Strategy.
"We are recommending an overweight position in both Hungary and Poland, the two best performing markets so far this year," strategist Nigel Rendell said.
"We also like Portugal while we believe that Turkey still provides some upside potential, particularly for the more trade-oriented investor."
Emerging Europe Europe includes Czech Republic, Greece, Hungary, Poland, Portugal and Turkey.

"We suggest that overweight positions in these four markets are financed at the expense of the Czech Republic and Greece, where a combination of economic concerns and poor liquidity in the former and lacklustre earnings growth in the latter will limit performance," it said.
The Hungarian market has been the star performer this year more than doubling in dollar terms the year to date, HSBC said.

"We still believe there is further upside over the medium term," it said, adding that an acceleration in GDP growth to up to three percent in 1997 from their estimate of around 1.5 percent this year will give support.
The Polish equity market has suffered from some profit-taking after its 1996 high, but "we see the longer run picture as encouraging," HSBC said.

It attributed its optimism to the continued buoyancy of the Polish economy. HSBC sees the economy growing five percent in 1997, on the back of the strength of domestic demand and some improvement in exports.
In Portugal, the country's ever greater progress to become part of mainstream Europe, is positive for the equity market.
While it is difficult to take longer term strategic positions on the Turkish market, HSBC said it was "cautioously optimistic on a medium term basis."
HSBC prefers emerging Europe over other assets after a strong regional performance in the first 10 months of the year, with the exception of Greece.
"The emerging European region as a whole is set to outperform the developed markets over the next 12 months," it said.

A combination of declining interest rates, stronger earnings growth as economic activity picks up in western Europe, attractive valuation and increasing foreign interest will be the main driving forces for equities in 1997, HSBC said.
